palette.notes: 14 colours measured, 2 ramps with tiny hue shift (2.4 deg). The finished art is one teal ramp on black; the tutorial UI is grey-mauve.

lighting: No drawn light: the source is filmed live footage, so light comes from the video, reduced to a teal monochrome ramp by dithering.
silhouette: A real hand cut out from green screen on black; the bright hand shape against black carries the whole read.

motion.timing: Holds median 100 ms, p75 191.7 ms (4.35 drawings/s), screen-recording steps. The result is a rotoscoped hand loop from live video.

texture: Error-diffusion dither over a tiny palette gives the Hylics-like crunchy, noisy surface.
camera: Screen recording of Aseprite with zoom on dialogs; each step gets one caption at the top.

acting.acts: No character: a step-by-step tutorial (import green screen clip, cut it out, shrink with linear interpolation, tiny palette, dither).
acting.depth: Flat UI; the result preview sits centred in the frame.

techniques: rotoscope live footage into pixel art
downscale with linear interpolation before quantising
really tiny colour palette, then error-diffusion dithering
one short caption per step on screen
result shown first as the hook, then the recipe
feel: result-first hook + one caption per step + tiny palette and dither = fast, copyable tutorial
for_fred: Open on the finished effect, then show the steps; and for a quick Fred gag, Robert can film a real motion, downscale and quantise it to Fred's ramp for weird, lifelike rotoscoped moves.
